newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU split on green rate compensation.
newsitem.headline: EU split on green rate compensation.

text.p: A plan to compensate European Union farmers for falls in their incomes due to revaluation of their "green rate" agricultural currencies has split member states, an EU member state official said on Wednesday.
The European Commission introduced the proposal to compensate British, Italian and Irish farmers hit by revaluation of their national currencies.
When currencies change, the green rate used to calculate EU farm payments is also adjusted.

"The proposal was discussed by the special agriculture committee on Tuesday but there was a solid minority against because a capping arrangement hits some countries and not others," the official said.
Under the proposal to be discussed by farm ministers at next week's agriculture Council, European Union payments would be limited to seven percent of income lost. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
